questions.stem: A pipeline must pass a load date to a notebook. How is this done?

options.text: Write the date to a text file in the lakehouse and have the notebook search the whole Files folder for it on each run
Mark a notebook cell as the parameters cell and set base parameters with the same names in the Notebook activity
Use a deployment rule on the notebook that sets the date variable in each stage
Hard-code the date in the notebook's first cell and edit it in the notebook before each pipeline run

questions.explanation: Values set as base parameters in the Notebook activity override the variables in the notebook's parameters cell when it runs.

questions.stem: A Copy activity must write to a folder named for today's date, such as 2026/11/03. Which dynamic expression builds the path?

options.text: @formatDateTime(utcNow(), 'yyyy/MM/dd')
FORMAT(GETDATE(), 'yyyy/MM/dd', 'en-US')
=TODAY()
${formatDate(currentDate(), 'yyyy/MM/dd')}

questions.explanation: Pipeline expressions start with @ and use functions such as utcNow() and formatDateTime().

questions.stem: A notebook must run five other notebooks, some in parallel and some after others, in one Spark session. What should it use?

options.text: notebookutils.notebook.runMultiple with a dependency graph
A deployment pipeline with one stage per notebook
A loop of %run magic commands started in five Python threads
Five separate pipelines, each with a Notebook activity

questions.explanation: runMultiple runs several notebooks in parallel or in a declared order within the same session.

questions.stem: A notebook run by a pipeline must return a row count to the pipeline. How?

options.text: Write the value into a markdown cell of the notebook, which the pipeline reads from the activity output
Print the value with print() and have the pipeline parse it from the Spark driver logs afterwards
Call notebookutils.notebook.exit with the value and read it from the activity's output in the pipeline
It isn't possible

questions.explanation: notebook.exit ends the notebook with a value that the pipeline reads from the Notebook activity's output with an expression.

questions.stem: A parent notebook calls notebookutils.notebook.run("LoadSales") and the child, which runs for about 10 minutes, keeps failing on a timeout. What should you change?

options.text: Move the child notebook to another workspace with a larger pool
Call notebookutils.notebook.exit in the parent before the run() call starts
Turn on high concurrency mode so the child gets its own session
Pass a larger timeout_seconds value, since the default is 90 seconds

questions.explanation: run() takes a timeout_seconds argument that defaults to 90 seconds, so a long child needs a larger value.

questions.stem: A child notebook calls notebookutils.notebook.exit(row_count) inside a try-except block, but the pipeline never receives the value. What is the fix?

options.text: Convert the value to an integer with int() before calling exit()
Call exit() at the top level of the code, outside the try-except block
Wrap exit() in a second, nested try-except block to catch and rethrow its error
Print the value before exit()

questions.explanation: exit() doesn't take effect inside exception handling and must be called at the top level, ideally in its own cell.

questions.stem: Before calling runMultiple, you call notebookutils.notebook.validateDAG on the DAG. Which two problems can it catch? Each correct answer is a complete solution.

options.text: Too little capacity to run the notebooks
Two activities with the same name
Circular references between activities
A cell in a child notebook with a syntax error
A child notebook that writes to the wrong table

questions.explanation: validateDAG checks the DAG's structure: duplicate names, missing dependencies and circular references. It doesn't run or inspect the notebooks' code.

questions.stem: A pipeline parameter myNumber is 42. A Set variable activity needs the string Answer is: 42. Which expression produces it?

options.text: @concat('Answer is: ', pipeline().parameters.myNumber
Answer is: @{pipeline().parameters.myNumber}
Answer is: @pipeline().parameters.myNumber
Answer is: @@{pipeline().parameters.myNumber}

questions.explanation: String interpolation wraps an expression in @{ } inside a string and returns a string. @@ escapes the @ so the expression isn't evaluated.

questions.stem: A pipeline runs several Notebook activities, and each waits for its own Spark session. You set the same session tag on each activity, but they still don't share a session. What else is required?

options.text: Turn on high concurrency mode for pipelines running multiple notebooks in the workspace settings
Give every Notebook activity identical base parameters so their Spark sessions can be matched by name
Put all the Notebook activities inside one ForEach activity with Sequential checked
Give each notebook a parameters cell that declares the session tag as a variable

questions.explanation: Session tags reuse an existing Spark session only when high concurrency mode for pipelines running multiple notebooks is turned on in the workspace's Spark settings.

questions.stem: A Copy activity's file name must be the literal text @export.csv, starting with the @ sign. How do you write it?

options.text: @{export.csv}
'@'export.csv
@@export.csv
@export.csv

questions.explanation: A value that starts with @ is treated as an expression. To get a literal string that starts with @, escape it as @@.
